messages:
Mia Chen: quick sync — proposal for handling cross-region handovers when a primary region drops below healthy capacity (GPU pool / sched failures). thinking we need a predictable, low-churn path that preserves streaming sessions where possible and limits DNS flapping.

Oliver Park: SGTM. important note: DNS flips won't move existing TCP/TLS streams, only new connections. for chat/streaming we need load-balancer-level draining + proxy handoff rather than pure GeoDNS.

Jamal Ortiz: also watch NAT port exhaustion for customers behind small NATs. if we suddenly route a lot of connections to a different egress, ephemeral port reuse could break long-lived flows. we saw this with apac->eu test last quarter.

Sasha Li: agreed. my rough proposal: 1) degrade region by priority instead of immediate failover 2) reduce GeoDNS TTL to 30s for new sessions but rate-limit updates 3) perform LB drain + proxy re-route for active streams 4) fallback to lower-memory model variant if GPU pressure persists. keeps tail latency bounded and cost predictable.

Ravi Patel: +1 to staged approach. couple of operational constraints: route53 latency-based records have propagation delay and client caching. lowering TTL helps but increases query QPS and cost. we should model the spike.

Oliver Park: example Route53 record update we would use for a priority flip (new sessions):
```
{
  "ChangeBatch": {
    "Changes": [
      {"Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": {"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-priority","TTL":30}}
    ]
  }
}
```

Mia Chen: operational runbook thoughts:
- detect: region unhealthy if GPU-healthy < 70% OR scheduling latency > 2s for 5m
- stage 0: mark region as degraded in control-plane metadata (no DNS changes)
- stage 1: lower TTL & start routing new sessions to secondary region at 10% ramp for 5m
- stage 2: if degradation persists, LB drain for stateful nodes and increase traffic to secondary to 100% for NEW connex only
- stage 3: if critical, switch GeoDNS priority and add rollback timer + automated mitigation (quantized model fallback)

Jamal Ortiz: important — mark the difference between NEW and EXISTING sessions in the change. we can't evict active KV caches; prefer migrating new requests. also add sticky cookie fallback for HTTP clients that support it.

InfraBot: Alert: eu-central GPU pressure test scheduled 2026-03-05T22:00Z. Will simulate 25% of traffic shift.

Sasha Li: we should run the canary with smaller TTL first (60 -> 30) and make sure our observability tracks: per-route P95 latency, open streams, NAT metrics, DNS QPS, and egress cost delta.

Ravi Patel: cost note — more frequent DNS churn and inter-region egress will increase bills. fallback strategy with quantized models can save ~30-40% GPU mem/cost during sustained failovers. include that in the rollout doc.

Mia Chen: next steps: Oliver to draft LB drain + proxy handover changes, Ravi to run cost model for TTL reduction scenarios, Sasha to create canary plan with metrics, Jamal to add NAT/runbook notes. I'll assemble into a short runbook and post for review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
